The #PNB Housing thesis has shifted from 'recovery' to 'structural re-rating' after the Q4 FY26 beat.

- With GNPA finally cracking the sub-1% barrier (0.93%) and the Roshni segment driving 32% YoY retail disbursement growth, the 11.8x PE still looks like a massive bargain compared to the 30x PE of high-growth peers. 
- Retail Growth: Retail disbursements hit an all-time high of ₹9,020 Cr in Q4.
  - Affordable Housing (Roshni): This segment is the growth engine, now at ₹8,150 Cr (a 61% YoY jump). 
The 'safety margin' is widening here as asset quality risk evaporates.

🏦The Valuation Arbitrage is clear:   
$BajajHousing trades at ~30x PE for its high-speed growth.
$PNBHousing is delivering similar momentum (PAT up 19%, Affordable segment up 61%) but still trades at just 11.8x PE.  
While $LICHousing remains the 'deep value' play.

⚡ PNB Housing has become the most compelling 'growth-at-a-reasonable-price' (GARP) pick in the sector. The safety margin here is built into the valuation gap. 📈🏠 

✅ The numbers have stopped whispering; they’re shouting. Whether the market listens now or at 15x is just a matter of time.

Shanti Gold Q4 FY26 – Strong Growth, But Look Deeper

At first glance, the numbers look exceptional:

• Q4 Revenue up 120% YoY, Volume up 15%
• FY26 Revenue up 80% YoY, Volume up 25%
Clearly, the company is gaining market share and benefiting from strong demand, supported by design capabilities and expanding clientele.

But the real story lies beneath the surface.

Shanti Gold is aggressively scaling capacity:
• Current: 2,700 kg
• Adding ~5,200 kg by July 2026 (~3x expansion)

This signals confidence and a clear intent to dominate scale.
However, FY26 profitability needs to be normalized.
The company used IPO proceeds to build gold inventory and did not hedge. With gold prices rising sharply, inventory gains directly boosted profits.

This led to:
• Elevated PAT margins (~7%+)
• Earnings that are not fully operational

Looking ahead:
• Revenue expected to grow 60–70%
• PAT margins guided at ~4%

This implies:
➡️ Revenues will grow
➡️ Profits may remain flat (~₹120–130 Cr)
➡️ EPS growth will be flat or slightly negetive

Key takeaway:
FY26 earnings are likely a peak due to one-off gains. The real story now shifts to execution — scaling volumes, maintaining margins, and delivering sustainable profitability.
